summary.intent: Make addrConn.connect() and updateAddrs() hold ac.mu across the state check and the hand-off to resetTransportAndUnlock, so two connection attempts cannot start in parallel (grpc-go#7365 flake, Test/AuthorityRevive).
summary.issue_fit: Full: the root cause in issue #7365 (mutex released between the idle check and resetTransport re-locking) is closed at both entry points; the supplied pull-request text is the only intent source and no commit-message promises beyond it.
summary.coverage: Complete diff (clientconn.go, one file) reviewed with its callers, the state-update path, balancer serializer and GracefulClose; two concurrency safety premises verified; focused tests run at head.
check_details: Reviewer ran `go test -count=1 -run 'Test/AuthorityRevive' ./xds/internal/xdsclient/tests/` at head 76ef33f: pass (single run; the 100000-run flake measurement in the supplied text was not repeated and is a supporting assertion only).

The idle-check/unlock/re-lock window described in issue #7365 is removed at connect() (clientconn.go:906-922); Test/AuthorityRevive passes at head

requirements.evidence: Not repeated: a 100000-attempt run exceeds the five-minute focused allowance; one run passed at head
clientconn.go:922 and 996 remove the parallel transport creation the note describes

tasks.premise: connect() and updateAddrs() never release ac.mu between validating state/ctx and resetTransportAndUnlock setting CONNECTING, and these are the only callers, so two overlapping connection attempts under one live ac.ctx cannot start.

updateAddrs returning with ac.mu held for the spawned resetTransportAndUnlock goroutine cannot deadlock with its deferred GracefulClose, because the goroutine reaches Unlock without waiting on the balancer serializer and updateState only enqueues.
